title: A degree-zero system identity passes through its specified limit square
statement: Let A be an abelian category with derived localizations of A and its strict towers. Let e:M[0]→M[0] have identity at every exact derived evaluation. For any functor L from D(towers A) to a category D, object K of D, isomorphism j:K≅L(M[0]), and f:K→K satisfying f≫j.hom=j.hom≫L(e), one has f=id. SingleTowerLimitWitness records precisely these objects, evaluation identities and square; its eq_id lemma is the bundled form.

source.place: paragraph (2), applying Rlim after equality in degree zero

proof.text: The degree-zero evaluation theorem gives e=id. A functor sends identity to identity. Substitute into the square and cancel the isomorphism j.

lean.statement:
theorem singleTowerLimitIdentity
    (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A)]
    {M : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A}
    (e : (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) 0).obj M ⟶
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) 0).obj M)
    (h : ∀ n : ℕ,
      ((evaluation ℕᵒᵖ A).obj (op n)).mapDerivedCategory.map e = 𝟙 _)
    {D : Type*} [Category D]
    (L : DerivedCategory (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ D) {K : D}
    (j : K ≅ L.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) 0).obj M))
    (f : K ⟶ K) (hf : f ≫ j.hom = j.hom ≫ L.map e) : f = 𝟙 K
